name: Converse with the hub in a plain terminal
principle: A person can converse with the hub in a plain terminal and always see what it is doing and what it asks.
state_description: Each line a person types is answered, the work behind each answer can be seen on request, every question the hub asks is shown where the person will see it and answered by the next line, and the session ends when the person leaves. While the AI works, each piece of information has one home: the live area shows what is happening now (running steps, helpers, elapsed time, cost, a message not yet taken up) and the scrolling transcript keeps what is finished and worth keeping, so nothing is shown in both at once and no old frame stays above the new one.
hints_of_measurement: Scripted sessions: every turn is answered, every question is answered, the session ends cleanly.

name: A terminal screen keeps the rules people settled on
principle: A terminal for working with the AI keeps every rule its users settled on over many rounds of use and any app on the hub gets them without rebuilding them.
state_description: A note typed while the AI works is the person's own line, counted until taken up, combined with the others into one next message, flushed by a stop, held back after an error and never sent as the answer to a question not yet read. A run ends in one closing line from structured fields only, with the metric before and after shown once above it. Warnings are one short line each with the rest in a log file. One clock and one elapsed format are used everywhere, with a clock at every wait over three seconds. The prompt is docked at the bottom, the transcript follows the newest output until the person scrolls away and selects by dragging, the keys that do something are listed whole, Ctrl+C copies or stops or asks twice to quit, text that carries information reaches 4.5 to 1 contrast, and everything fits 80 columns with no sideways scrollbar.
hints_of_measurement: Scripted sessions on a fake worker that emits contract events: each rule has a test, and the arm passes the same scripted sessions as the other arms.
